name: DIY canthoplasty

lead: DIY canthoplasty is the practice of cutting the outer corner of one's own eyes at home to lengthen the eye opening and tilt the corner upward, imitating the effect of cosmetic lateral canthoplasty. Photos and guides have circulated on looksmaxxing forums and short-video platforms, and the aim is the longer, more upturned eye shape associated with a positive canthal tilt.

Surgeons describe lateral canthoplasty as an operation that divides and repositions the lateral canthal tendon under sterile conditions, not simply an incision of the corner. Posters of forum guides themselves include warnings against attempting it.

paras: Forum posts describe the idea in general terms and show before-and-after photos; the wiki does not reproduce steps. Authors often note that the corner partly heals back, and that revision is possible.

Reported or described risks include infection, scarring, asymmetry, blunting or rounding of the corner, dry eye, lid malposition and, in the worst case, injury to the eye. Some forum authors warn that it can cause blindness. Surgeons say outcomes from formal canthoplasty are limited by anatomy and that revision is difficult.

angle.text: Practitioners seek a longer, more upward-set outer eye corner. Surgeons note the effect depends on anatomy and that the tendon work in a real operation is what repositions the corner.

lead: DIY canthoplasty is the self-performed alteration of the lateral canthus, the outer corner where the upper and lower eyelids meet. The aim is to imitate cosmetic lateral canthoplasty, which is sought for a lifted, elongated look sometimes called a fox eye [1][2].

Within looksmaxxing communities, the motive is the eye area: a longer palpebral fissure and a more upward-tilted outer corner are discussed as attractive features. Forum threads have shown results photographed months afterward, with authors noting that a cut corner can heal back partly [3].

Medical sources describe canthoplasty as surgery of the medial and/or lateral canthus [1], and surgeons describe the formal procedure as dividing and repositioning the lateral canthal tendon, with canthopexy a gentler tightening of the same tendon [2]. Published literature covers the professional procedures; no study has examined self-performed versions.
infobox: Infection, scarring, asymmetry, lid malposition, eye injury

paras: Lateral canthoplasty in a surgical setting lifts and lengthens the outer eye corner, sometimes alongside a brow lift. One Australian surgeon's overview says that the surgeon divides and repositions the lateral canthal tendon, in contrast to canthopexy, which suspends it, and that the fox-eye label is a social-media term rather than a clinical one [2]. It also notes that bony orbit shape and existing canthal position limit how much change is achievable [2].

Threads on looksmax.org discuss self-performed versions, with at least one poster describing results four months later and noting that the corner had partly healed back [3]. The posts are accompanied by disclaimers warning readers about blinding themselves [3]. Other threads have debated why the practice became a trend.

For professional canthoplasty, a surgeon overview lists asymmetry as the most common aesthetic complaint, plus blunting of the canthal angle, webbing, scleral show, ectropion or lid retraction, dry eye, scarring, infection, hematoma and, rarely, visual disturbance. It says revision is technically harder than the original operation and that results are assessed after six to twelve months [2]. Forum posters have described self-performed cuts as 'mutilation' [3].

lore.intro: Self-performed canthoplasty is discussed on looksmax.org through guides, photo threads and debates, often with disclaimers [3].
